ML Ratchet · Wildfire Phase 2 · project 2

FireSize

A wildfire has just been reported. Will it be caught small, or run past 100 acres? FireSize answers from the ignition record, the landscape around it and two days of weather. It learned only from simulated fires, then was graded once on real US ignitions.

Eight ignitions from the exam, picked by a fixed random draw within size classes. The network runs in your browser. Change the weather or the record and watch the size distribution move. The black tick is what really happened.

Lab: change the inputs

Weather sliders move the discovery day and the day before together. Moving fuel dryness (ERC) also moves 100-h and 1000-h fuel moisture and the burning index along the dev-fitted relation. Landscape stays that of the real ignition.

How a simulated fire gets its size

Each training fire is ignited in a real 18 km LANDFIRE window under real gridMET weather and spread by FireSim (Rothermel surface fire, crown fire, minimum-travel-time spread on a 90 m grid) for four days with no suppression. That gives a free-burn area curve.

Suppression is a race, as in Fried & Fried (1996): crews arrive after a response time and build line; the fire is contained when the line built catches up with the line needed around its perimeter. Its final size is the area at that moment. Below is one simulated dev twin. Drag the sliders.

The ratchet

A rung is kept only if it beats the incumbent on the frozen simulated set by more than 0.01 ranked probability skill and does not lose more than 0.01 escape AUC or 5 % size error on the dev gate (half of the 8,913 dev ignitions, never used for calibration). Every rung was re-scored on the latest frozen set.

Use it

The release firesize-v1.0.zip holds numpy-only inference, the weights, a demo on eight exam ignitions, the model card and every training script.

import firesize
m = firesize.FireSize()
out = m.predict(features)        # pandas DataFrame with the 75 input columns
out["p_escape"], out["median_acres"], out["interval80_acres"]

The landscape inputs come from 250 m national LANDFIRE grids (training/natgrid.py rebuilds them in a few minutes); weather inputs are gridMET daily values. See the model card for each column.
